name.text: Using logarithms to determine the age of an archeological sample

questiontext.text:
An archaeologist studies an ancient sample containing carbon-14. The percentage \(P\) of carbon-14 remaining in the sample is modelled by

\(P=100\left(\frac12\right)^{t/5730}\),

where \(t\) is the age of the sample in years.

Laboratory analysis shows that {@P@}% of the original carbon-14 remains. Use logarithms to calculate the age \(t\) of the sample in years.

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]][[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked solution

Step 1: Start with the carbon-14 decay equation.

The percentage of carbon-14 remaining is modelled by \(P=100\left(\frac12\right)^{t/5730}\), where \(t\) is the age of the sample in years.

Step 2: Divide both sides by 100.

\(\frac{P}{100}=\left(\frac12\right)^{t/5730}\).

Step 3: Take natural logarithms on both sides.

\(\ln\left(\frac{P}{100}\right)=\ln\left(\left(\frac12\right)^{t/5730}\right)\).

Using the logarithm rule \(\ln(a^b)=b\ln(a)\), we obtain

\(\ln\left(\frac{P}{100}\right)=\frac{t}{5730}\ln\left(\frac12\right)\).

Step 4: Rearrange to make \(t\) the subject.

Multiply both sides by 5730 and divide by \(\ln\left(\frac12\right)\):

\(t=5730\frac{\ln(P/100)}{\ln(1/2)}\).

Step 5: Substitute the given percentage.

\(t=5730\frac{\ln({@P@}/100)}{\ln(1/2)}\).

Therefore, the estimated age of the sample is

\(t={@t@}\text{ years}\).

Final answer:

\( \boxed{t={@t@}\text{ years}} \)
